_meta.indication: Prophylaxis of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) which may lead to pulmonary embolism (PE) in patients undergoing knee or hip replacement surgery.

pivotal_trials.design: International, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-control (enoxaparin), parallel-group
pivotal_trials.population: Patients undergoing elective hip replacement surgery
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Composite of total VTE (any DVT, non-fatal PE, or death from all causes) at end of treatment
pivotal_trials.result: Total VTE 1.1% (18/1595) rivaroxaban vs 3.7% (58/1558) enoxaparin; ARR 2.6%, p<0.0001

pivotal_trials.design: International, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-control (enoxaparin); extended rivaroxaban (35 days) vs enoxaparin (13 days)
pivotal_trials.population: Patients undergoing elective hip replacement surgery
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Composite of total VTE at end of treatment
pivotal_trials.result: Total VTE 2.0% (17/864) rivaroxaban vs 9.3% (81/869) enoxaparin; ARR 7.3%, p<0.0001

nct_ctgov.title: Regulation of Coagulation in Orthopedic Surgery to Prevent DVT and PE, a Controlled, Double-blind, Randomized Study of BAY 59-7939 in the Extended Prevention of VTE in Patients Undergoing Elective Total Hip Replacement

pivotal_trials.design: International, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-control (enoxaparin), parallel-group
pivotal_trials.population: Patients undergoing elective knee replacement surgery (TKR)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Composite of total VTE at end of treatment
pivotal_trials.result: Total VTE 9.6% (79/824) rivaroxaban vs 18.9% (166/878) enoxaparin; ARR 9.3%, p<0.0001

nct_ctgov.title: Regulation of Coagulation in Orthopedic Surgery to Prevent Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT) and Pulmonary Embolism (PE). A Study of BAY 59-7939 in the Prevention of VTE in Subjects Undergoing Elective Total Knee Replacement.

pivotal_trials.phase: Multi-center randomized controlled trial (data integrity concerns deemed unreliable by FDA)
pivotal_trials.design: International, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy; enoxaparin 30 mg twice daily (US regimen)
pivotal_trials.population: Patients undergoing elective knee replacement surgery (TKR)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Composite of total VTE at end of treatment
pivotal_trials.result: Total VTE 6.9% (67/965) rivaroxaban vs 10.1% (97/959) enoxaparin; ARR 3.2%, p=0.012; however FDA concurred that the RECORD 4 information appears unreliable and cannot be used for an approval decision.

nct_ctgov.title: Regulation of Coagulation in Orthopedic Surgery to Prevent Deep Vein Thromboembolism (DVT) and Pulmonary Embolism (PE). A Study of BAY59-7939 in the Prevention of Venous Thrombo Embolism (VTE) in Subjects Undergoing Elective Total Knee Replacement.

key_safety: The major risk is bleeding. In the RECORD studies, major bleeding was higher with rivaroxaban (24, 0.39%) than enoxaparin (13, 0.21%), including one fatal GI bleed with rivaroxaban. Common adverse reactions (≥1%) in RECORD 1-3 included wound secretion (2.8%), pruritus (2.1%), pain in extremity (1.7%), blister (1.4%), muscle spasm (1.2%) and syncope (1.2%).
target_moa: Rivaroxaban is an orally bioavailable, selective factor Xa inhibitor that blocks the active site of factor Xa without requiring a cofactor (such as antithrombin III), inhibiting thrombin formation and the coagulation cascade.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: SURGICAL SETTINGS—SPINAL/EPIDURAL HEMATOMA. Epidural or spinal hematomas may occur in anticoagulated patients receiving neuraxial anesthesia or undergoing spinal puncture, and may result in long-term or permanent paralysis.

advisory_committee.vote: Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee (March 19, 2009) voted 15 (yes) to 2 (no) that the data demonstrate a favorable risk-benefit profile for rivaroxaban in VTE prophylaxis after hip or knee replacement surgery.

description.text: Added treatment of DVT, treatment of PE, and reduction in the risk of recurrence of DVT and of PE

citations.quote: These "Prior Approval" supplemental new drug applications provide for the treatment of deep vein thrombosis, the treatment of pulmonary embolism, the reduction in risk for deep vein thrombosis and the reduction in risk for pulmonary embolism.

description.text: Added a new 10 mg once-daily dosing regimen to reduce risk of recurrent DVT and/or PE in patients at continued risk after at least 6 months of initial treatment

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the new dosing regimen of 10 mg once daily for the reduction in the risk of recurrence of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and/or pulmonary embolism (PE) in patients at continued risk for DVT and/or PE after completion of initial treatment lasting at least 6 months.

description.text: Added new indication for prophylaxis of venous thromboembolism in acutely ill medical patients at risk for thromboembolic complications not at high risk of bleeding

citations.quote: The Prior Approval supplemental new drug application for NDA 022406 provides for a new indication for the prophylaxis of venous thromboembolism in acutely ill medical patients at risk for thromboembolic complications not at high risk of bleeding.

summary.text: Standard full approval of an oral factor Xa inhibitor for DVT/PE prophylaxis after hip or knee replacement surgery, supported by four RECORD trials; the application went through two review cycles after a May 27, 2009 complete response letter and was discussed at a Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee that voted 15-to-2 in favor.

citations.quote: This new drug application provides for the use of Xarelto® (rivaroxaban) 10 mg immediate release Tablets, for the prophylaxis of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism in patients undergoing: hip replacement surgery or knee replacement surgery.
The applicant was sent a complete response letter on May 27, 2009. The applicant responded to the complete response letter on January 4, 2011.

The Committee voted 15 (yes) to 2 (no) that the available clinical data demonstrate a favorable risk-benefit profile for rivaroxaban in the prophylaxis of venous thromboembolism in patients undergoing hip or knee replacement surgery.

requirement.text: PMR 1797-1: A postmarketing pharmacovigilance study of the risk factors, clinical management, and outcome of cases of major bleeding in association with Xarelto (rivaroxaban) use.

citations.quote: PMR 1797-1 A postmarketing pharmacovigilance study of the risk factors, clinical management, and outcome of cases of major bleeding in association with Xarelto® (rivaroxaban) use.

requirement.text: PMR 1797-2: Perform a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of renal impairment plus concurrent use of P-gp and moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors on the PK, PD, and safety of rivaroxaban to develop appropriate dosing recommendations.

citations.quote: PMR 1797-2 Perform a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of renal impairment (i.e., mild, moderate, severe) plus the concurrent use of P-gp and moderate inhibitors of CYP3A4 on the pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and safety of rivaroxaban in volunteers so that appropriate dosing recommendations can be developed in these populations.

requirement.text: PMC 1797-3: Develop and propose a 5 mg strength tablet or scored 10 mg tablet to allow for proper dose titration when rivaroxaban is co-administered in patients at risk for clinically relevant changes in rivaroxaban exposure.

citations.quote: PMC 1797-3 Develop and propose a 5 mg strength tablet or scored 10 mg tablet to allow for proper dose titration when rivaroxaban needs to be co-administered in patients at risk for clinically relevant changes in rivaroxaban exposure.
The December 30, 2010, submission constituted a complete response to our May 27, 2009, action letter.

basis.text: Need to clarify chemistry, manufacturing and control issues, additional understanding of potential safety issues, and additional clarification of data integrity issues.

citations.quote: However the application could not be approved during the first cycle due to the need to clarify chemistry, manufacturing and control issues, need for additional understanding of potential safety issues and need for additional clarification of data integrity issues.
